---
title: "Penrose Tiling"
---

``` {ojs}

canvas = {
  const S = config.size;
  const concurrency = config.concurrency;
  const context = DOM.context2d(S, S);
  paper.setup(context.canvas);
  paper.view.viewSize = new paper.Size(S, S);

  const lines = data.lines.reverse();
  let paths = [];
  let i = 0;
  let fillColor;
  const reset = () => {
    paper.project.activeLayer.removeChildren();
    const backgroundLayer = new paper.Layer();
    const background = new paper.Path.Rectangle(paper.view.bounds);
    const colorIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * config.colors.length);
    fillColor = fillColorByArea(config.colors[colorIdx]);
    background.style = { fillColor: config.colors[colorIdx].bgColor };
    paper.view.draw();
    i = 0;
  };
  const animate = lines => {
    paths = [];
    i = 0;
    const b = bounds(lines);
    const scaleX = d3
      .scaleLinear()
      .domain([b[0], b[2]])
      .range([10, S - 10]);
    const scaleY = d3
      .scaleLinear()
      .domain([b[1], b[3]])
      .range([10, S - 10]);
    return () => {
      if (i > lines.length / concurrency) return;
      for (let batch = 0; batch < concurrency; batch++) {
        const pos = batch * Math.floor(lines.length / concurrency) + i;
        if (!lines[pos]) continue;
        const path = new paper.Path({
          segments: [],
          strokeColor: 'white'
        });
        lines[pos].forEach(point => {
          path.add(new paper.Point(scaleX(point.x), scaleY(point.y)));
        });
        if (Math.abs(path.area) < 10) continue;
        path.fillColor = fillColor(path);
        paths.push(path);
      }
      i++;
    };
  };
  reset();
  context.canvas.onclick = reset;
  paper.view.onFrame = animate(lines);

  return context.canvas;
}

config = {
  return {
    size: 600,
    concurrency: 4,
    colors: [
      { bgColor: '#E1DAD2', scheme: ['#FF4400', '#F7DA00', '#07748C'] },
      { bgColor: '#FED322', scheme: ['#20BA4E', '#F20775', '#51358C'] },
      { bgColor: '#F2EFC7', scheme: ['#FF9D83', '#4071A6', '#D3DEE8'] }
      // { bgColor: '#101115', scheme: d3.schemePastel1 },
      // { bgColor: '#fefefe', interpolator: d3.interpolatePlasma },
    ]
  };
}

data = linedata(L(parse(penroseLSystem)), 5)

<!-- md` -->
<!-- Click the canvas to reset the tiling and pick a random color scheme from the ones available in config. Change the config object to increase the size or experiment with different color schemes.  -->

<!-- We use an L-System to generate the lines of the Penrose tiling. The logic to compute lines is imported from [this awesome interactive l-system explorer](/@kelleyvanevert/l-systems-2). I've re-written the rendering to work with canvas and paperjs and I've added fill colors to the shapes in the tiling. -->
<!-- ` -->

penroseLSystem = `order: 5
axiom: [N]++[N]++[N]++[N]++[N]
angle: 36
colorful

M -> OF++PF----NF[-OF----MF]++
N -> +OF--PF[---MF--NF]+
O -> -MF++NF[+++OF++PF]-
P -> --OF++++MF[+PF++++NF]--NF
F ->`

<!-- md`## Dependencies` -->

fillColorByArea = colors => {
  let scale;
  if (colors.interpolator) {
    scale = d3
      .scaleSequential()
      .domain([240, 720])
      .interpolator(colors.interpolator);
  } else if (colors.scheme) {
    scale = d3.scaleOrdinal(colors.scheme);
  }
  let vals = new Set();
  return path => {
    const val = Math.abs(Math.round(path.area));
    vals.add(val);
    return scale(val);
  };
}

import { bounds, parse, L, linedata } from '@kelleyvanevert/l-systems-2'

d3 = require('d3@v5')

paper = require('paper')
```
